case.pattern_description: Coordinated multi-card fraud syndicate utilizing a specific mobile device (Samsung SM-G935F) operating behind an anonymous IP proxy to execute unauthorized online purchases across dozens of unrelated cardholder accounts. The device consistently registers as New on each victim account while evading individual transaction scoring thresholds. The modus operandi exactly mirrors confirmed fraud cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3467346 on card C01289-K1 generated a low model score of 0.027 with a historical fraud rate of 0.006 and legacy risk score of 0.15.
Flagged transaction 3467346 originated from device D004630, which was marked as New for cardholder account C01289-K1 and operated behind an anonymous IP proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

Device D004630 is an anchor device in fraud ring 36700632 and was used across 18 distinct cards in the 30-day window (29 transactions across 20 cards in +/-7 days), appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy on every card.

Device D004630 is directly implicated in four prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035), where victims reported unauthorized card-not-present transactions executed from this exact device profile behind an anonymous proxy under an undocumented fraud pattern.

Card C01289-K1 has an established baseline consisting almost exclusively of in-person purchases (24 of 25 transactions, all in product category W), making an online purchase for product C from a new device an abrupt departure from established cardholder behaviour.
Flagged transaction 3467346 was billed in region 472, matching the billing region of all 25 prior transactions on card C01289-K1.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: On November 18, 2016, transaction 3467346 ($89.53) on card C01289-K1 was flagged during monitoring due to its association with device D004630 and fraud ring 36700632. Although automated risk models scored the transaction low, graph analysis revealed that device D004630 has been utilized across 18 cards in a 30-day window and is directly linked to four prior confirmed-fraud cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035). Card C01289-K1 had established a consistent baseline of in-person purchases in product category W, making this online transaction in product category C an abrupt behavioral departure. The alert was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated multi-card syndicate, leading to case creation, analyst escalation, monitoring of 17 connected cards, and regulatory reporting.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details suspected card-not-present fraud conducted by an organized multi-card syndicate involving customer C01289 and primary card C01289-K1. On November 18, 2016, at 10:59:00 UTC, flagged transaction 3467346 for $89.53 was executed in the online channel for product category C in billing region 472. The transaction originated from mobile device D004630, identified by user agent string "SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080", operating behind an anonymous IP proxy. Device D004630 appeared as a new device on card C01289-K1, departing sharply from the cardholder's prior established profile of 24 in-person retail transactions in product category W. Internal network graph analysis confirmed that device D004630 serves as an anchor device in fraud ring 36700632 and has transacted across 18 distinct payment cards within the preceding 30 days, including cards C09906-K1, C01996-K2, and C04108-K2. The modus operandi across all connected accounts involves registering device D004630 as a new mobile device behind an anonymous IP proxy to execute unauthorized online purchases while evading automated fraud scoring thresholds. Furthermore, device D004630 is directly tied to four prior confirmed-fraud investigations (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035), where cardholders formally disputed identical unauthorized online charges. The identified direct financial exposure on card C01289-K1 is $89.53. In response, the institution has flagged the affected transaction, escalated the syndicate activity for analyst intervention, initiated monitoring on 17 connected cards, and submitted this report under Bank Rules R6 and R9.

stop_reason: Under policy section 6, the investigation was concluded because multiple independent lines of decisive evidence—specifically cross-card links and prior confirmed fraud cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035 tied to device D004630—established a fraud probability of 0.343, and further investigative steps would not alter the required escalation and reporting actions.
